heroSummary: The Creality K1 Max handles Overture TPU 95A exceptionally well straight out of the box thanks to its tight dual-gear direct drive extruder. Print speeds must be capped at 54 mm/s to strictly enforce the material's 4.5 mm³/s maximum volumetric flow rate and prevent extruder jams.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate + Glue Stick release agent
slicerTweaks: Cap Maximum Volumetric Speed to 4.5 mm³/s under the Filament > Advanced settings tab to inherently prevent under-extrusion and filament buckling.
Disable Pressure Advance or tune it to a low baseline (around 0.04s) to prevent erratic extruder motor movements on compliant TPU.
Enable 'Avoid Crossing Walls' and set 'Max Detour Length' to reduce unnecessary retractions and nozzle wiping movements across open perimeters.
Reduce print acceleration to 2500 mm/s² across all features to maintain consistent toolhead pressure on this flexible filament.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Filament wrapping around extruder drive gears
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive volumetric flow rate or print speed exceeding 54 mm/s causing high backpressure in the meltzone.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Enforce the 4.5 mm³/s volumetric speed limit in OrcaSlicer and loosen extruder tension screw slightly if overly compressed.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing and fine webbing across open gaps
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Filament moisture absorption causing steam expansion inside the hotend, or insufficient wipe distance.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool at 55°C for 6 to 8 hours and enable 2.0 mm wipe distance with 0.8 mm retraction at 30 mm/s.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Build plate surface damage / permanent bonding
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: TPU chemically bonding to the PEI coating due to direct contact at elevated temperatures without an interface barrier.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a uniform layer of PVP glue stick to the textured PEI sheet to serve as a sacrificial release agent before starting the print.

faq.question: Can I feed Overture TPU 95A through the stock Creality K1 Max reverse Bowden tube?
faq.answer: Yes, but it is recommended to bypass the rear spool holder and mount the dry box directly overhead to minimize friction through the long PTFE tube.

faq.question: Should the top glass cover and front door be kept closed while printing TPU?
faq.answer: No, it is advisable to remove the top glass lid or prop the door open to avoid heat creep inside the enclosed chamber, which softens TPU before the gears.

faq.question: Why does TPU require a glue stick if bed adhesion is already high?
faq.answer: Glue stick acts as a release barrier rather than an adhesive; without it, TPU fuses with PEI coatings and can rip the sheet upon part removal.

faq.question: Can I use OrcaSlicer's input shaping calibration for Overture TPU 95A?
faq.answer: Yes, but ensure you test input shaping at the lower 54 mm/s operating speed range, as elastomeric materials behave differently under high vibration.
